ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the graphs of the linear functions $y=kx$ and $y=mx+n$ are shown as in the figure. What is the solution set of the linear inequality in one variable with respect to $x$, $(k-m)x-n>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From $(k-m)x-n>0$, we obtain: $kx>mx+n$,\\
According to the graph, the intersection point of the two functions is $(1, 2)$,\\
Therefore, the solution set of the linear inequality in $x$, $kx>mx+n$, is $x>1$, that is, the solution set of the linear inequality in $x$, $(k-m)x-n>0$, is $\boxed{x>1}$.
